the-story-this-serves.text: A registry integrator keeps using the state validator already deployed.
The story demands the same script hashes, acceptances, refusals, trace reasons and transaction effects after the source is divided into owners.
The promise is checked by comparing all eleven validators of a fresh blueprint, field by field, with the blueprint from before the move.
And by comparing all three hundred sixty Aiken tests, three hundred forty of which report a cost, on status, memory and CPU cost, and traces, under the same property seed.
Both comparisons ran after each of the four moves, and again on the final tree, and found no difference.

one-owner-per-rule.text: A diagram is shown here: the state module dispatches minting to genesis, custody spends to custody, and Modify spends to the modify owner.

The modify owner runs the fold, checks each duty through discharge, and settles lovelace through settlement. The fold collects duties and asks the trie owner for its refusals. Discharge and settlement read custody outputs.

Dependencies run one way, from the dispatch down; no owner imports the state module, and refusal, duty, trie and genesis import no other owner. A change inside a lower owner needs no edit above it while its exported names and types stay the same.
Every moved declaration kept its body byte for byte, importing its names unqualified.

Aiken has no re-export, so two test modules now call the trie and retirement refusals in their owners directly, and every test's measured cost is unchanged. A forwarding function was not built or measured.

how-a-fold-is-judged.text: A diagram is shown here of the order in which a Modify is judged.
First the continuation address, state token, no drain and preserved pins. Then the fold over every input: carriage, phase, edge, approval and trie move.

Then the batch checks: something consumed, no surplus action, the root, and the mint delta. Then each duty is discharged, and finally custody refunds, positional refunds and each payee's sum are settled.
The first failing check is the one reason traced, and that order is part of the contract.

what-each-owner-holds.text: A table is shown here with ten owners, each linked to its source.
The state module dispatches. Genesis mints the state token. Modify owns the judging order and the frame refusals such as continuation address, state drain, root and net mint mismatch.
The fold owns carriage, phase, edge admission and approval refusals. The trie owner names the leaf refusals such as key unknown, not booked and edge from terminal.

Duty only collects. Discharge refuses a wrong destination, absent custody, a missing burn and a missing token. Settlement refuses a short refund or a returned deposit. Custody refuses a custody spend outside its fold. Refusal reports.

where-a-common-change-goes.text: A table is shown here routing seven common changes to the owner to edit.

A new request check goes to the fold; a new edge to the fold and duty; token destinations to discharge; lovelace payments to settlement; custody spending to custody; the check order to modify; booting to genesis.
Any change that moves a compiled script moves its hash, the manifest, the witness pin and every deployment on the old hash. That is a deployment decision, never a side effect of reorganizing source.

documentation-in-the-aiken-source.text: Each owner documents itself in Aiken doc comments: responsibility, dependencies, assumptions and invariants, plus a description on every public declaration and on the validator.
The onchain flake check named aiken docs enforces this over an extent it discovers, on the source at any indentation the compiler accepts, and on the reference the pinned Aiken generates.

On the generated reference it reads each module's members off the page and reconciles them with the source inventory both ways, so a member the source reading missed still fails without a description.

It then plants each kind of gap in a copy, including an indented undocumented function, and requires each layer to refuse it for that reason; it accepts the same function once documented, and shows the reconciliation refusing a mismatch in either direction.
The check establishes presence, not truth; no doc comment is evidence of what the validator does.

the-generated-reference.text: The site publishes the reference the pinned Aiken docs command generates from these doc comments, built from the same revision as the rest of the site. Each owner's name in the table opens its generated page, and each member's view source link opens the lines it documents, at the commit the site was built from.

The diagram follows the path: the doc comments become generated pages, their source links are bound to the built commit and the onchain directory, and a manifest records the digests the documentation check compares.

Every validators module that declares a public definition has a page. Test and property modules are not documented, and the open approval policy, the staking validator and the vector table declare nothing public, so their sources are the reference.

The check refuses a missing reference, a page or source that no longer matches its recorded digest, a module without its page, a source link to another repository, revision or line, a script loaded from off the site, or this page no longer linking it. Each refusal is planted in a scratch copy on every run, and must be refused for that reason.

evidence-and-limits.text: The identity and cost comparisons ran against the revision before the move, after each of the four moves and on the final tree, and found nothing changed.
From here on, the continuous integration carriers keep the promise: the script identity manifest, the Aiken suite, the vectors, and devnet journeys on a fresh blueprint.

Limits: property tests report no cost, so their evidence is outcome, iterations and counterexample under the fixed seed; the comparison proves preservation, not correctness, which stays the Lean model's question.

The Aiken configuration that names the repository in the source links also sets the blueprint's description; correcting it changed that description and no validator's compiled code or hash, as the script identity check confirms. And the documentation check proves each description exists, not that it is accurate.
